title: Rubies and sapphires are the same mineral: a trace of chromium makes the red

cover.alt: The Logan Sapphire: a huge, deep blue cushion-cut gemstone surrounded by a ring of small diamonds, against a blue background.
cover.credit: Chip Clark, Smithsonian staff · Public domain

body: Both gems are [corundum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corundum), a crystalline form of aluminium oxide, Al₂O₃. The crystal on its own is transparent; its colours come from traces of other elements caught in its structure. When chromium is present the stone is red, and **red corundum is called ruby**. Corundum of every other colour, from blue to yellow, green, orange and purple, is sold as sapphire. Either way it is extremely hard, scoring 9 on the Mohs scale, which makes it the third-hardest mineral after diamond and moissanite.

steps.label: Traces of other elements enter the crystal
With chromium it turns red: a ruby
Other colours are all called sapphire

slides.prompt: A corundum stone is pink. Is it a ruby or a sapphire?
slides.answer: It depends on where you are
slides.detail: In the US a stone needs a minimum colour saturation to count as a ruby; paler ones are pink sapphires. Other places draw the line differently.

slides.alt: Five rough corundum crystals on white cloth: one pale yellow, one clear, one pale green and two pinkish purple.
slides.caption: Rough corundum crystals in a range of colours, each set by traces of different elements in the same aluminium oxide.

slides.label: the Logan Sapphire, about 85 g of blue corundum
slides.text: It is one of the largest faceted gem-quality blue sapphires in existence, and is on show at the National Museum of Natural History in Washington, D.C.

slides.heading: From gems to gadgets
slides.text: In 1902 the French chemist Auguste Verneuil announced a way to make synthetic ruby crystals, and blue sapphire followed in 1909. Synthetic sapphire is now used for scratch-resistant watch crystals and small windows, and as the base for gallium nitride in blue LEDs.

slides.question: What gives blue sapphire its colour?
slides.explanation: The blue comes from intervalence charge transfer: an electron moving between iron and titanium ions in the crystal changes the charge on both.
